title: Comparative latency vs cost — spiralboard draft (Apr 2026)
content:
Executive summary:

This note collects a set of small, focused experiments comparing latency percentiles and estimated unit cost for three representative workload shapes. The goal is to produce short collateral (1–2 slides worth) that product/SDR can use when discussing performance tradeoffs with customers and internal sales. This is a working draft: numbers are from synthetic replay and limited live-traffic experiments on the staging cluster (r3) — treat as directional, not canonical.

Key takeaways (quick):
- For interactive chat traffic (short turns, high turns-per-session) a light prewarm (warm pool size = 1 per GPU) reduces p99 by ~22% with a 4–6% cost overhead depending on amortization window.
- For batched embeddings the dominant lever is batching window; increasing window from 10ms->50ms yields ~2.8x throughput improvement and 30–40% CPU/GPU amortized cost drop, but p90 latency increases by ~28ms.
- Long-form single-shot generation (1k+ tokens) shows that KV-cache-aware packing reduces per-query token cost by ~18% without changing p50; p99 benefits only if packing reduces scheduler preemption.

Testbed and methodology:
- Cluster: staging-r3 (4x A100-80GB partitions, mixed MMIO kernel selection on 2 nodes).
- Runtime: runtime v0.73-rc (PR 3145 linked above), quantization baseline: fp16 for all runs.
- Measurement tool: replay harness (replay-cli v1.2) to feed recorded session traces and a synthetic generator for embeddings. Each experiment ran for 20 minutes after a 5-minute warmup.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 latency (end-to-end, client-observed), tokens/sec, requests/sec, GPU utilization, inferred cost per 1k tokens (using internal cost model: gpu-hour -> $X normalized to token units).
- Error bounds: single-run variability ~3–6% for p50/p90, up to 12% for p99 on microburst scenarios.

Workload shapes:
1) Interactive chat (short turns): 80–120 tokens per turn, 8–12 turns per session, inter-turn gap 300–800ms. 1000 concurrent sessions.
2) Embeddings bulk: batches of 32 texts, average 150 tokens input, arrival Poisson (mean 200 qps).
3) Long gen single-shot: 1 request = ~1k tokens output, concurrent 40 requests.

Results (compact):
- Chat (baseline vs light-prewarm vs aggressive-prewarm):

| mode             | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | cost per 1k tokens ($) |
|------------------|----------|----------|----------|------------------------:|
| baseline (on-demand) | 78       | 210      | 420      | 0.028                  |
| light-prewarm     | 72       | 185      | 330      | 0.029                  |
| aggressive-prewarm | 70       | 175      | 300      | 0.033                  |

ASCII p99 bars (relative length, shorter = better):
baseline:  █████████████████████████████████████████ (420)
light-prewarm: ████████████████████████████████ (330)
aggressive-prewarm: ███████████████████████████ (300)

Observations: prewarm reduces p99 substantially; cost delta is small for light prewarm (<6%) but grows with aggressive policies. For customer-facing collateral emphasize "~20% p99 improvement at ~<5% cost increase" use-case.

- Embeddings (10ms vs 50ms batching window):

| window(ms) | throughput (qps) | p90 (ms) | cost per 1k tokens ($) |
|------------|------------------:|---------:|------------------------:|
| 10         | 2,100             | 45       | 0.021                  |
| 50         | 5,900             | 73       | 0.013                  |

Tradeoff note: batching window from 10->50ms increases throughput ~2.8x and reduces per-token cost ~38% but p90 increases ~28ms (customer-visible). Customer guidance: for throughput-first workloads choose 50ms+ with optional per-route override for low-latency customers.

- Long-form generation (packing/no-packing):

| mode     | tokens/output | p50 (ms) | p99 (ms) | cost per 1k tokens ($) |
|----------|---------------:|---------:|---------:|------------------------:|
| no-pack  | 1200           | 1100     | 3100     | 0.095                  |
| pack-KV  | 1200           | 1082     | 2640     | 0.078                  |

Note: pack-KV reduced p99 when preemption contention drops because packing allows longer steady GPU kernels and fewer context-switches.

Short narrative visuals (for slide copy):
- Slide 1: "Small prewarm, big p99 win" — bullet: "~22% p99 reduction for chat; cost delta ~+4%". Add mini-table from chat.
- Slide 2: "Batching window trades latency for per-token cost" — include simple two-bar chart with throughput and p90 overlay (throughput increases, p90 shifts right).
- Slide 3: "Packing benefits long-form workloads" — show per-token cost drop and reduced p99.

Practical guidance (what to recommend to customers):
- Interactive chat SaaS: enable light prewarm for premium tiers; expose control as fraction-of-gpu-pool or prewarm-count per route. Keep default conservative.
- Bulk embeddings: expose batching window knob in Console (10/25/50/100ms presets) with recommended profiles (throughput/cost/latency).
- Long-form generation: enable packing-aware scheduling for routes with >512 tokens output or >10s expected runtime.

Caveats & open questions:
- Cost numbers are modelled from internal gpu-hour -> token conversion; need finance validation for public collateral.
- Tests were on fp16 and A100-80GB kernels; customer hardware (e.g., H100 or quantized int8) will shift absolute numbers.
- p99 variability on microburst patterns still high; consider adding 95% CI bars to final slide.

Action items (short):
- [INF-7890] run replicate on r4 cluster (H100) and validate relative deltas (owner: Nina).
- finalize slide deck with visuals and two canned customer anecdotes (owner: Marcus).
- pass cost numbers to Finance for sign-off before external use (owner: Liam).

Appendix — raw sample numbers (single-run snapshots):
chat-baseline: p50=78ms p90=210ms p99=420ms qps=1700 tokens/s=35k gpu_util=62% cost_1k=0.028
chat-light-prewarm: p50=72ms p90=185ms p99=330ms qps=1680 tokens/s=34.6k gpu_util=65% cost_1k=0.029
emb-10ms: throughput=2100 qps p90=45ms gpu_util=48% cost_1k=0.021
emb-50ms: throughput=5900 qps p90=73ms gpu_util=84% cost_1k=0.013
long-nopack: p50=1100ms p99=3100ms tokens_out=1.2k cost_1k=0.095
long-packkv: p50=1082ms p99=2640ms tokens_out=1.2k cost_1k=0.078

Testing commands (staging):
- chat replay: replay-cli run --trace traces/chat-short-turns.json --concurrency 1000 --ramp 60 --runtime-tag spiralboard-apr02
- embeddings: replay-cli run --pattern embeddings-bulk.json --batch-window 50 --concurrency 200
- long-gen: replay-cli run --pattern long-gen.json --concurrency 40 --pack-kv on

References and links:
- JIRA: INF-7890 (regression and cross-cluster validation)
- PR: runtime#3145 (kernel-selection improvement used in tests)
- Slack: #observability (thread: Apr 2 performance sketch)

Notes to self: when converting to slide, avoid raw per-token $ values — use percentage deltas and relative bars unless Finance signs off. Also capture a short customer quote from one beta tenant that observed p99 improvements with light prewarm (if permission granted).
